title: 2026-09-27 Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Elm Transport
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on expanding reserved capacity, adding EU region availability, and negotiating a 12-month contract extension. Customer wants a performance benchmark in eu-west for peak routing traffic, clarity on KMS/data residency, and a final pricing sheet for 2x reserved GPU capacity plus burst. Redwood to run a perf run and share updated pricing and SOC2 docs. Next steps agreed: benchmark, pricing, legal timeline and follow-up demo of cross-region failover.
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~40m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Elm CTO), Aisha Patel (Head of MLOps), Tom Reyes (VP Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check-in, how's it going at Elm since our last call?
[00:12] Liam: Hey Jordan, good to see you. Busy month, we're ramping up shipments and traffic spiked in August, so capacity's been the main topic internally.
[00:20] Aisha: Yeah, hi. We're seeing 1.8x token growth month-over-month on the routing models, and the burst windows are killing our latency targets.
[00:31] Jordan: Right, great context. Today I wanted to walk through options for reserved capacity increase, adding eu-west region for lower latency to our EU customers, and the contract/extension timing so we can lock pricing. Priya's on to talk perf.
[00:45] Priya: Hi folks, thanks. Quick note: the plan we demoed was on Redwood Dedicate - sorry, Redwood Dedicated - with reserved GPU pools. For the 2x capacity scenario we typically recommend bumping the burst pool and also enabling cross-region KV cache replication for EU traffic.
[01:05] Tom: When you say KV cache replication, do you mean like an in-region cache copy, or a global cache with failover?
[01:12] Priya: Good question. We usually do prefix/KV cache per region to reduce tail latency; you can do async replication for warm-up but primary access should be region-local. It avoids cross-AWS-region hops.
[01:25] Liam: Cool. From security perspective, we need KMS integration and logs forwarded to our SIEM. Are those covered under Redwood Private or Dedicated?
[01:34] Jordan: KMS and audit logs are supported for both Dedicated and Private. Dedicated gives you isolated pools and customer-managed KMS via our integration; Private adds a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC. Marcus can chime on the log forwarding options.
[01:46] Marcus: Yep, we can send audit logs to your S3 or Splunk endpoints, support SAML/SSO and RBAC mapping. We also have SOC2 artifact links we can share.
[01:55] Aisha: We actually need the SOC2 Type II and a note on data residency for EU jobs. Also, our legal team will want a clause about not moving model logs out of region.
[02:05] Jordan: Understood. We'll attach SOC2 and our data residency spec. For the contract, are you looking to extend the current term or sign a new 12-month reserved commit?
[02:14] Tom: Ideally new 12-month commit so we can get the better per-token and reserved pricing. We'll probably want to double the reserved capacity and add eu-west as a billed region.
[02:24] Jordan: Great. Pricing wise that maps to a 2x reserved discount plus per-region surcharge for EU. I'll update the pricing sheet.
[02:30] Priya: To be concrete on perf, we should run a benchmark in eu-west for the production model you use. Aisha, can you confirm which model and peak RPS?
[02:38] Aisha: We're on the open-roberta-lite variant for reranking and a small T5 derivative for summarization. Peak for rerank is around 180 req/s in the 15-min burst, avg is 60.
[02:48] Priya: Nice. For 180 RPS with short sequences we can show sustained latency under 120ms p95 on a 4-GPU pool with batching and prefix caching, but we'll validate with your exact payloads.
[02:59] Liam: One more: multi-region failover. If eu-west is up but us-west has an outage, what's the expected failover impact?
[03:06] Priya: There will be increased tail latency because of cold KV misses and cross-region traffic until caches warm. We can architect an active-passive failover with warm rehydratation to keep the hit small, and Redwood's smart routing can prefer regions by policy to minimize cost.
[03:20] Tom: That sounds acceptable. Do you have a runbook or playbook for the failover?
[03:25] Marcus: Yes, we have a runbook and a cross-region failover demo we can schedule. I'll send the link.
[03:32] Jordan: Let's walk timeline. Aisha to share monthly token usage and regional split; Priya to schedule benchmark in eu-west; Jordan to send pricing and SOC2/docs; Marcus to send runbook and logs integration notes.
[03:45] Aisha: Quick question on billing: if we add eu-west, do we get a single invoice with region breakdown or separate invoices?
[03:52] Jordan: Single invoice with per-region line items. If you do a contract extension we'll reflect reserved commitments across regions.
[03:58] Liam: Legal will need standard indemnity and data residency language. We might need a redline but that's downstream.
[04:05] Jordan: Totally. We'll start with our standard amendment and you can redline.
[04:09] Tom: Can we get a formal SLAs doc? Our ops team expects 99.9% for reserved pools.
[04:15] Marcus: Our Dedicated SLA for reserved pools is 99.9% monthly uptime. I'll attach the SLA PDF and the escalation matrix.
[04:23] Aisha: One risk we flagged: model quantization changes. If Redwood recommends a quantized variant to save cost, we need to ensure quality regression checks. Do you have eval hooks?
[04:33] Priya: We do. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles and we can run a prompt-set regression check; we can attach the eval scorecard so you can gate rollouts.
[04:40] Liam: Ok good. On the performance benchmark — we need it on our payload with our headers and auth flow. Aisha will share a sanitized subset. When can you run it?
[04:49] Priya: Earliest next week. If you can share traffic samples by Thursday we'll run a 180 RPS 20-minute run across eu-west.
[04:58] Aisha: Thursday works.
[05:00] Jordan: Pricing — I'll send two SKUs: 2x reserved (12-month) and 2x reserved plus eu-west addition. I'll include burst pool and a 10% transit surcharge estimate for cross-region egress, and KMS cost.
[05:12] Tom: About KMS, do we have to bring our own key or can Redwood manage keys?
[05:17] Marcus: Both options. For Dedicated you can bring your own key via KMS integration and we never persist plaintext keys. For Private we support HSM options as well.
[05:26] Liam: Great. If we choose BYOK, what's the audit trail like?
[05:30] Marcus: We produce key usage logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM, and we include an entry in the audit events for every decryption request.
[05:38] Aisha: Ok that's sufficient for legal. One more ask: can you show cost forecasts for the next 12 months if traffic grows 2x? We need to budget for holiday spikes.
[05:48] Jordan: Yes, I'll put a forecast into the pricing spreadsheet with three scenarios: baseline, +25%, +100% (2x).
[05:55] Tom: On timeline for contract signature, we want the new pricing to kick in November 1st if possible. Can you work to get numbers and legal language by Oct 7th?
[06:03] Jordan: We can target Oct 7th for draft amendment. Benchmarks and perf data by Oct 1. Does that timeline work for you?
[06:10] Liam: Yes.
[06:12] Aisha: Yes.
[06:14] Jordan: Alright, quick live Q&A for Priya — any technical blockers you foresee for the eu-west roll?
[06:20] Priya: Not really. Depending on model size we'll pick quantization profile and kernel selection. The main friction is prefix cache warm-up across regions; to mitigate, we recommend a staged rollout with synthetic warmers and pre-population. Also watch out for tokenization differences if you have EU customers using different encodings.
[06:39] Tom: About tokenization, we do have a small subset using legacy encoding for certain partners; will that affect batching?
[06:45] Priya: It can. Different token lengths affect batch composition; we'll set batching policies per route so it won't degrade tail latency.
[06:54] Marcus: I'll note that in the runbook for the benchmarking team.
[07:00] Jamie (interrupting, off mic): Sorry, I just joined, Jamie from Elm legal — do you have a sample amendment we can review?
[07:06] Jordan: Hi Jamie, yes we do. Jordan: we'll share the draft amendment and a redline template.
[07:11] Jamie: Thanks.
[07:13] Jordan: Ok final recap: Aisha to share sanitized traffic samples and monthly token usage by 2026-09-30; Priya to run eu-west benchmark by 2026-10-01 and deliver perf report; Jordan to send updated pricing and forecast and SOC2 and SLA by 2026-10-04; Marcus to send runbook and log/KMS integration notes by 2026-10-01; legal draft by 2026-10-07.
[07:35] Liam: Appreciate it. One last ask: can we get a short demo of the cross-region failover behaviour before we sign? Ideally a 20-min demo with our ops team watching.
[07:44] Priya: Yep we can schedule a failover demo the week after the benchmark.
[07:49] Tom: Sounds good.
[07:52] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the deliverables.
[07:58] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional ASR glitches ("Redwood Dedicate"), and some names may be slightly off, but content reflects action items and next steps agreed on call.
